reviewMethod: Antigravity drafts separately reviewed against complete archived version bodies and source notes; source discrepancies retained explicitly.

headings.title: Permitted commodity associations and single-commodity limit
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 and history note (RSMo 1939 § 14377; prior revision 1929 § 12719). Authorizes incorporation of seven named growers' associations while prohibiting forming any such association for more than one of those commodities, and allows incorporation of associations for other unnamed commodities or products of the soil; retains archived semicolon punctuation ("associations of growers; or producers").

headings.title: Required inclusion of commodity name in corporate name
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 and history note. Requires every chapter 275 association to include in its corporate name the name of the commodity its members grow, produce, and market (or propose to).

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read both subsections and history/prior-revision notes (RSMo 1939 § 14377; 1929 § 12719) and verified source/text/subsection fingerprints. Checked seven enumerated growers' associations, single-commodity limit on those associations, allowance for unnamed soil commodities (retaining archived semicolon "associations of growers; or producers"), and required commodity name in the corporate name. Retained both titles as accurate.

headings.title: Capital stock divided into par or no-par shares
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 and history note (RSMo 1939 § 14371; prior revision 1929 § 12713). Requires chapter 275 associations to have capital stock divided into par-value or no-par-value shares as determined by the incorporators in their articles of association; retains archived opening word "That".

headings.title: Ten-to-one-hundred-dollar par value and issuance price range
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 and history note. Sets a $10 to $100 per-share range for both par-value shares and the issuance price of no-par-value shares as determined in the articles of association.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read both subsections and history/prior-revision notes (RSMo 1939 § 14371; 1929 § 12713) and verified source/text/subsection fingerprints. Checked capital stock division into par or no-par shares (retaining archived opening word "That") and the $10 to $100 range for both par value and no-par issuance price set in articles of association. Retained both titles as accurate.

headings.title: Director duties after receiving a council establishment petition
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 including subdivisions (1) to (7), paragraphs (a) to (d) of subdivision (4), continuation sentences in (4)(d), and history note (L. 1969 S.B. 65 § 5, A.L. 1973 S.B. 92, A.L. 1977 S.B. 330, A.L. 1979 S.B. 43). Lists seven director steps upon receiving a commodity merchandising council petition, including publishing notice in at least three agricultural publications of 75,000+ statewide circulation at least one month before the hearing with publication fees advanced in cash by the representative group (no state funds).

headings.title: Deadlines for sufficiency review, hearing notice, and registration
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 and history note. Requires determining petition sufficiency within twenty-one days and publishing notice giving at least ten days' notice prior to public hearing and thirty days' notice to register prior to the referendum; notes archived textual tension with the one-month pre-hearing notice stated in subsection 1(4)(d).

headings.title: Referendum adoption thresholds by voters and production
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 3 and history note. Establishes dual adoption thresholds: a majority of votes cast in favor and favorable voters representing a majority of the production of all registered producers casting votes; distinct from the director's declaration in subsection 4.

headings.title: Director declaration of proposal adoption
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 4 and history note. Directs the director to declare a petition proposal adopted once the required percentages by number and by production of voting producers are in favor; distinct from the thresholds stated in subsection 3.

headings.title: Fee or major changes and council fee adjustments
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 5 and history note. Covers initiating fee-change or other major-change proposals (two-thirds council vote or twenty-five percent producer petition) requiring a referendum with original dual thresholds, plus the exception allowing a council by two-thirds vote to lower fees or restore them up to the originally approved rate without a referendum, effective only at the start of the next state fiscal year.

headings.title: Termination proposals and simple-majority referendum
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 6 and history note. Allows proposing program termination by a majority of the council or a petition of ten percent of registered commodity producers, decided by a simple majority of those voting in a referendum.

headings.title: Twelve-month waiting period between similar commodity referendums
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 7 and history note. Prohibits holding a referendum to establish a council, change fee amounts, make other major changes, or terminate a council within twelve months of a referendum for a similar purpose for the same commodity.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read all seven subsections including subdivisions (1) to (7), paragraphs (a) to (d) and continuation sentences in (1)(4)(d), and history note (L. 1969 S.B. 65 § 5, A.L. 1973 S.B. 92, A.L. 1977 S.B. 330, A.L. 1979 S.B. 43), and verified source/text/subsection fingerprints. Checked the archived internal notice-period tension between at least one month's pre-hearing publication notice in subsection 1(4)(d) and at least ten days' pre-hearing notice in subsection 2 (retained without silent reconciliation), dual voter/production thresholds versus director declaration, council fee-adjustment exception effective next fiscal year, simple-majority termination, and 12-month waiting period. Retained all seven titles as accurate and well-differentiated.

headings.title: Public hearings, permanent record, and director determination
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 and history note (L. 1969 S.B. 65 § 4, A.L. 1973 S.B. 92). Requires every hearing under sections 275.300 to 275.370 to be public with a permanent record of all testimony, conducted by an administrative hearing officer with the director authorized to make the determination from the record.

headings.title: Published findings and delivery of decisions to parties
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 and history note. Directs the director to make and publish findings based on hearing facts, testimony, and evidence and have copies of findings and decisions delivered or mailed to all parties of record or their attorneys of record.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read both subsections and history note (L. 1969 S.B. 65 § 4, A.L. 1973 S.B. 92) and verified source/text/subsection fingerprints. Checked public hearings under sections 275.300 to 275.370, permanent testimony record, administrative hearing officer role, permissive director determination from the record, published findings, and delivery or mailing of findings and decisions to parties or attorneys of record. Retained both titles as accurate.

headings.title: Fee collection by councils, director contracts, and transfers
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 and history note (L. 1969 S.B. 65 § 7, A.L. 1998 H.B. 1876 merged with S.B. 945). Directs appropriate commodity councils to collect program fees directly from producers or indirectly from handlers/processors, authorizes contracting with the director under subsection 5, and directs the director to transfer collected fees to the director of revenue.

headings.title: Late penalties, civil collection actions, and one-year limitation
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 and history note. Imposes a one-percent-per-month penalty on unpaid merchandising fees, authorizes civil collection suits (with costs on defaulting payers) brought by the attorney general or a requested county prosecuting attorney, and sets a one-year statute of limitations.

headings.title: Commodity council merchandising fund creation and non-lapse
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 3 and history note. Creates the Commodity Council Merchandising Fund for administration fees paid under section 275.370, requires general assembly appropriation to the department of agriculture for program administration, and exempts unexpended balances from lapse under section 33.080.

headings.title: July 10, 1998 revisions excluded from 275.330 major changes
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 4 and history note. Declares that the revisions to the commodity merchandising councils act made by section 275.350 and effective July 10, 1998, are not deemed a major change for purposes of section 275.330.

headings.title: Director collection contracts, nonstate funds, and monthly distribution
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 5 including subdivisions (1) and (2) and history note. Authorizes director-council contracts to collect, audit, and administer checkoff funds (retaining only service costs into the merchandising fund), treats all other fees as nonstate funds administered by the director of revenue under Mo. Const. Art. IV, § 15 with inspectable records, and requires monthly distribution by the tenth day of each month less refunds, while distributing national assessment funds pursuant to law.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read all five subsections including subdivisions (1) and (2) of subsection 5 and history note (L. 1969 S.B. 65 § 7, A.L. 1998 H.B. 1876 merged with S.B. 945) and verified source/text/subsection fingerprints. Checked council collection and director contract transfers, 1%/month penalty, civil collection suits and one-year limitation, Commodity Council Merchandising Fund creation and section 33.080 non-lapse, July 10, 1998 exclusion from section 275.330 major changes, and Mo. Const. Art. IV, § 15 nonstate-fund administration and 10th-of-month distribution. Retained all five titles as accurate.

headings.title: State fee cap and refund exemption upon federal assessment
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 and history note (L. 1988 S.B. 785 § 1, A.L. 2015 S.B. 12). Limits state fees if a federal beef assessment passes to no more than a commensurate amount credited against the federal obligation, and exempts beef from the section 275.360 refund provision upon adoption of the federal assessment; read alongside subsections 2 and 10.

headings.title: Post-August 28, 2015 referendum prerequisite for state fees
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 and history note. Notwithstanding subsection 1, allows a beef commodity council to collect state fees only if a referendum is approved on or after August 28, 2015, under subsections 3 to 12.

headings.title: Beef checkoff petition, fee cap, and referendum duties
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 3 including subdivisions (1) to (7), paragraphs (a) to (c) of subdivision (4), continuation sentences in (4)(c), and history note. Covers council (two-thirds vote) or producer (twenty-five percent) petitions to impose or modify a Missouri beef checkoff fee capped at the federal assessment and seven director duties, including notice in agricultural publications totaling 225,000+ statewide circulation at least one month before hearing, paid in advance in cash by the council.

headings.title: Deadlines for sufficiency review, hearing notice, and registration
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 4 and history note. Requires determining petition sufficiency within twenty-one days and publishing notice giving at least ten days' notice prior to public hearing and thirty days' notice to register prior to referendum; notes archived textual tension with the one-month pre-hearing notice in subsection 3(4)(c).

headings.title: Referendum adoption thresholds by voters and production
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 5 and history note. Establishes dual adoption thresholds: a majority of votes cast and favorable voters representing a majority of the production of all registered producers casting votes; distinct from the director's declaration in subsection 6.

headings.title: Director declaration of proposal adoption
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 6 and history note. Directs the director to declare the petition proposal adopted once the required percentages by number and by production of those voting are in favor; distinct from the thresholds in subsection 5.

headings.title: Fee or other changes and council fee adjustments
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 7 and history note. Covers initiating fee or other change proposals (two-thirds council vote or twenty-five percent producer petition) requiring a referendum with original dual thresholds, plus council two-thirds vote authority to lower or restore fees up to the originally approved rate without a referendum, effective only at the start of the next state fiscal year.

headings.title: Termination proposals and simple-majority referendum
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 8 and history note. Allows proposing termination of the Missouri beef checkoff fee by council majority or ten-percent registered beef producer petition, decided by a simple majority of those voting in a referendum.

headings.title: Twelve-month waiting period between similar fee or major-change referendums
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 9 and history note. Bars holding a referendum to change the fee amount or make other major changes within twelve months of a referendum conducted for a similar purpose (note that unlike section 275.330(7), this subsection does not expressly list initial setup or termination referendums).

headings.title: Collection manner, separate accounting, and section 275.360 refunds
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 10 and history note. Requires collecting section 275.352 fees in the same manner as the federal beef assessment, requires separate department accounting for state and federal assessments, and makes state fees collected under this section subject to section 275.360 refunds (contrasting with subsection 1).

headings.title: Remittance to Missouri Beef Industry Council and fund uses
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 11 and history note. Notwithstanding section 275.350, requires remitting fees under section 275.352 to the Missouri Beef Industry Council for deposit in a separate account, restricted exclusively to researching, marketing, educating, and promoting beef products and production.

headings.title: Rulemaking authority, chapter 536 compliance, and nonseverability
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 12 and history note. Grants permissive department rulemaking and policy/form/guideline authority, subjects rules (as defined in section 536.010) to chapter 536 and section 536.028, and makes the section nonseverable from chapter 536 so that invalidation of general assembly review, delay, or annulment powers voids rulemaking authority and rules proposed or adopted after August 28, 2015.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read all twelve subsections including subdivisions (1) to (7), paragraphs (a) to (c) and continuation sentences in (3)(4)(c), and history note (L. 1988 S.B. 785 § 1, A.L. 2015 S.B. 12), and verified source/text/subsection fingerprints. Checked subsection 1 federal-assessment cap and section 275.360 refund exemption alongside subsection 2's post-August 28, 2015 referendum prerequisite and subsection 10's separate accounting and section 275.360 refundability for state fees; verified the internal pre-hearing notice tension between subsection 3(4)(c) (one month) and subsection 4 (ten days), subsection 9's narrower 12-month waiting period, subsection 11 remittance to the Missouri Beef Industry Council, and subsection 12's chapter 536 nonseverability clause and post-August 28, 2015 voiding trigger. Retained all twelve titles as accurate and well-qualified.

headings.title: Definitions for section 275.357
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 including subdivisions (1) to (5) and paragraphs (a) and (b) of subdivision (4), plus history note (L. 2022 1st Ex. Sess. H.B. 3; effective 1-02-23). Defines council (referencing section 275.300 and Missouri Soybean Merchandising Council), federal act (7 U.S.C. § 6301 et seq.), handler (including Commodity Credit Corporation loan forfeitures), net market price, and processor (including producer-processors).

headings.title: State assessment when federal rate is one-half percent
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 and history note. Sets the state soybean assessment under section 275.350 at half of the 0.5-percent federal assessment while the federal rate remains 0.5 percent of net market price, clarifying that it corresponds to the state credit/portion paid to the council and is not in addition to the national assessment.

headings.title: State assessment if federal rate drops or ends
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 3 and history note. Establishes the fallback state assessment if the federal assessment drops below 0.5 percent or ceases to be effective: 0.5 percent of net market price of Missouri-grown soybeans less any assessment paid to the United Soybean Board under the federal act.

headings.title: Collection and remittance of combined state and federal assessments
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 4 including subdivisions (1) and (2) and history note. Requires the combined state and federal assessments to be collected and remitted to the council by the handler or processor first acquiring the producer's soybeans, or remitted by a producer-processor marketing processed products of the producer's own soybeans.

headings.title: Applicability of section 275.360 refunds to state fees
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 5 and history note. Makes state fees collected under section 275.357 subject to the refund provision of section 275.360.

headings.title: Exclusion from 275.350 fee changes and 275.330 major changes
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 6 and history note. Specifies that section 275.357 shall not be construed as changing any fee collected under section 275.350 or as a major change for purposes of section 275.330.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read all six subsections including subdivisions in subsections 1 and 4 and history/effective-date notes (L. 2022 1st Ex. Sess. H.B. 3; effective 1-02-23) and verified source/text/subsection fingerprints. Checked definitions (section 275.300 and 7 U.S.C. § 6301 et seq.), conditional state soybean assessment when the federal rate equals 0.5% versus when it drops below 0.5% or ends, combined assessment collection/remittance by handlers/processors/producer-processors, section 275.360 refunds, and exclusion from section 275.350 fee changes and section 275.330 major changes. Retained all six titles as accurate.

headings.title: Council officers, expenditure authorization, and program duties
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 including subdivisions (1) to (3) and history note (L. 1969 S.B. 65 §§ 6, 8). Directs each commodity merchandising council to elect a chairman and desired officers, authorize the director with council approval to expend a budgeted amount from the commodity council merchandising fund for program administration and fee collection, and perform other duties prescribed in the program.

headings.title: Council advice to director on collections, audits, and refunds
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 and history note. Directs the director to be guided by the commodity merchandising council's advice, recommendations, and assistance in fund collection, audits, and refunds. Independent review revised title to include "audits" alongside fund collections and refunds so all three statutory subjects are represented.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read both subsections including subdivisions (1) to (3) and history note (L. 1969 S.B. 65 §§ 6, 8) and verified source/text/subsection fingerprints. Checked council officer elections, budgeted merchandising-fund expenditure authorization, program duties, and director guidance by council advice/recommendations/assistance across collections, audits, and refunds. Revised subsection 2 to include "audits" alongside collections and refunds; retained subsection 1.

headings.title: Council creation, districts, qualifications, terms, and vacancies
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 and history note (L. 1989 H.B. 214 § 275.455). Creates the five-member Missouri Aquaculture Council elected by commercial producers (four district members from department-drawn districts and one at-large member), states citizenship, residency, one-year voter, and sections 275.452–275.455 producer qualifications (noting archived wording "preceding their appointment" despite elected status), sets three-year terms with staggered initial terms, and provides for filling unexpired vacancies.

headings.title: Mandatory reimbursement of members' actual and necessary expenses
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 and history note. Mandates ("shall be reimbursed") reimbursement of actual and necessary expenses incurred by council members in performing their duties; contrasts with permissive reimbursement in section 275.462(2). Independent review revised title to make explicit the mandatory "shall be reimbursed" phrasing in direct contrast with permissive reimbursement under section 275.462(2).

headings.title: Council duties, fund administration, officers, and bylaws
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 3 including subdivisions (1) to (6) and history note. Lists six council duties: providing a commercial fish producer list to the department of agriculture, administering the aquaculture marketing development fund, electing officers, adopting bylaws, communicating with producers on fish market development, and other necessary duties.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read all three subsections including subdivisions (1) to (6) and history note (L. 1989 H.B. 214 § 275.455) and verified source/text/subsection fingerprints. Checked five-member elected Missouri Aquaculture Council creation, four districts plus one at-large seat, qualifications (retaining archived "preceding their appointment" wording), staggered initial terms, mandatory ("shall be reimbursed") expense reimbursement contrasting with section 275.462(2), and six statutory duties. Revised subsection 2 to make mandatory reimbursement explicit; retained subsections 1 and 3.

headings.title: Quarterly fish-food purchase reports and charge payments
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 and history note (L. 1989 H.B. 214 § 275.450 subsecs. 3, 4). Requires commercial producers to file signed duplicate quarterly reports on fish-food purchases and accompanying charge payments with the director of agriculture on or before January 15, April 15, July 15, and October 15; notes archived phrasing "charges provided in this section" although the per-ton charge is set in section 275.452.

headings.title: Fine for unpaid charges on section 275.452 fish-food purchases
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 and history note. Subjects any commercial producer who purchases fish food mentioned in section 275.452 to a fine of $50 to $1,000 unless the charge imposed by sections 275.452 to 275.455 is paid. Independent review revised title for tighter neutral phrasing while retaining the exact section 275.452 cross-reference and nonpayment condition.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read both subsections and history note (L. 1989 H.B. 214 § 275.450 subsecs. 3, 4) alongside section 275.452 context and verified source/text/subsection fingerprints. Checked duplicate quarterly reporting and payment deadlines (January 15, April 15, July 15, October 15), retained archived phrasing "charges provided in this section" (originating when sections 275.452 and 275.455 were subsections of H.B. 214 § 275.450) without silently altering the source, and verified the $50 to $1,000 fine referencing section 275.452 fish food. Revised subsection 2 for tighter neutral phrasing; retained subsection 1.

headings.title: Council creation, qualifications, staggered terms, and vacancies
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 and history note (L. 1998 H.B. 1240). Creates the five-member Missouri Wine Marketing and Research Council elected by commercial producers, requires Missouri citizenship, residency, and commercial-producer status, sets three-year terms with staggered initial one-, two-, and three-year terms, and provides for filling unexpired vacancies by election.

headings.title: Permissive reimbursement of members' actual and necessary expenses
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 and history note. States permissive ("may be reimbursed") reimbursement of actual and necessary expenses incurred by council members in performing their duties; contrasts with mandatory reimbursement in section 275.450(2).

headings.title: Council duties, fund administration, officers, and bylaws
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 3 including subdivisions (1) to (6) and history note. Lists six council duties: providing a commercial wine producer list to the department of agriculture, administering the Missouri wine marketing and research development fund, electing officers, adopting bylaws, communicating with producers to enhance enology research, education, and Missouri wine market development, and other necessary duties.
